## Context / Problem

Implement only the lifecycle/ownership shape approved by the runner research story. This is a behavior-preserving ownership refactor plus any fault-proven correctness fixes; it is not a line-count exercise.

## Approach

- Add the fault-matrix tests before movement.
- Move cohesive call-graph clusters into the existing owner selected by the research, or introduce one adequately sized sibling only if no existing owner fits.
- Preserve one provider-resource owner, fallback model close-before-provider close ordering, failure spend/step accounting, answer-model attribution, success logging before potentially-raising finalization, final usage/run-shape/spend updates, and provider provenance.
- Replace string monkeypatch/re-export dependencies with narrow injection only where the same change migrates every consumer.
- Record before/after method/module measurements as evidence, never as a gate.

**Licensed outcome, reverified against the CURRENT tree (post-prerequisite):** the prerequisite
[rebar:patriotic-valued-hog] already concluded, with a full effect/resource boundary timeline
and consumer census, that "no restructuring of `run()`'s ownership is warranted right now" —
every extracted concern already has exactly one owner in `agent_call.py`/`providers.py`/
`model_classes.py`/`structured_run.py`/`runner_support.py`, and `run()`'s remaining lines are
irreducible orchestration glue, not a movable cluster. Re-inspecting the current tree for this
ticket confirms that conclusion still holds (file sizes/complexity checked fresh, see Testing).
**"No code movement, confirm the fault matrix, add the one uncharacterized fault-matrix
boundary this ticket's own Testing section names, done" is therefore a licensed outcome for
this ticket — exactly as "no restructuring, evidence-only" was licensed for the prerequisite —
not a shortfall against the Approach above.** The Approach's movement bullets are conditional
on a movable cluster existing; none does.

**fe75 disposition:** the prerequisite's research also found one genuine gap — a raise inside
`_findings.finalize_outcome` (runner.py, outside both the `ProviderSession` `with`-block and
the failure-accounting `try/except`) skips `record_call_spend`/`interpret_failure`/
`step_failures.record`. That gap was filed as its own ticket, `fe75-a4a3-9eef-457c`
(discovered_from this research), which is now `in_progress` with its RCA already complete and
a fix already designed there. Fixing it is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for 6586 to avoid two
concurrent changes racing on the same `runner.py`/`test_pydantic_ai_runner.py` lines; 6586
instead adds the one still-uncharacterized fault-matrix boundary from its own Testing list
that fe75 does NOT cover: a "telemetry failure" (`setup_tracing` swallowing a configured-but-
failing OTLP/Langfuse setup, not merely the no-keys no-op case already pinned).

## Scope

- Only the runner-cluster files named by the prerequisite's approved ownership map [rebar:patriotic-valued-hog].
- Focused runner/provider/cache/fallback/telemetry tests in `tests/unit/` and `tests/interfaces/`.
- No project-wide policy, config-schema, provider API, or workflow-engine change.

## Testing

Start with the prerequisite's full fault matrix. Exercise a normal structured call, text call, fallback success, provider/capability failure, external-call failure after usage, finalization failure, and telemetry failure. Compare result/provenance/accounting shapes before and after; run the default suite plus lint/typecheck/complexity/module-size gates.

All boundaries except "telemetry failure" already have fault-matrix coverage landed by prior
tickets (a49e, c465): `tests/unit/test_provider_session_guard.py` (provider-session raise/close
ordering), `tests/unit/test_llm_fallback_chain.py` (fallback-chain raise/close-once ordering),
`tests/unit/test_llm_failure_matrix.py` (provider/output classification matrix),
`tests/unit/test_pydantic_ai_runner.py::test_a_raise_in_finalize_outcome_still_logs_but_skips_the_spend_row`
(finalization-failure boundary, current-gap-pinning, owned going forward by fe75). This ticket
adds `tests/unit/test_tracing.py::test_setup_tracing_swallows_a_configured_setup_failure`,
proven RED (against a same-session mutation removing the swallow: `TracerProvider()` raises,
test fails for that reason) then GREEN restored, for the telemetry-failure boundary the
Testing section names but nothing previously drove (the sibling no-keys test never reaches
`setup_tracing`'s second `try/except`, the one guarding actual provider/exporter construction).

Before/after measurements (evidence, not a gate): file sizes unchanged since c465
(runner.py 788, agent_call.py 435, structured_run.py 602, providers.py 344, model_classes.py
621, runner_support.py 153 — all within the 800 hard cap); `check_complexity_baseline.py
--check` reports `active=39 new=0 increased=0 stale=10`, unchanged by this ticket's test-only
diff.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every fault-matrix test fails against the deliberately broken ordering/cleanup variant it guards and passes on the implementation. (Verified for the new telemetry-failure test in this ticket via a same-session mutation/restore; the other boundaries were teeth-proven in a49e/c465 and re-run green here unchanged.)
- [x] Provider clients and fallback-owned clients close exactly once in the established order on success and every injected failure path. (Unchanged; no code moved; existing `test_provider_session_guard.py`/`test_llm_fallback_chain.py` still pass.)
- [x] Failed calls retain failure spend and step-failure accounting; successful calls retain answer attribution, pre-finalization log semantics, final result shape, usage, and spend. (Unchanged; the one known gap — finalize_outcome-raise skips the spend row — is tracked and being fixed in fe75, not duplicated here.)
- [x] The implementation follows the research-approved owner map and deletes superseded orchestration; it does not duplicate `ProviderSession`, `ExitStack`, settings builders, telemetry helpers, or provider/capability selection. (No code moved — the research-approved map is "no move"; nothing superseded to delete; nothing duplicated.)
- [x] Every moved string/monkeypatch consumer is migrated in the same change; no compatibility re-export is retained solely to hide a broken test seam. (Vacuously satisfied — nothing moved.)
- [x] No function-size ratchet, per-file headroom check, hook/plugin bus, mechanically split sub-100-LOC module, or padding is added. (Confirmed — only one new test function added.)
- [x] Default suite, focused runner/provider/cache/fallback/telemetry tests, lint, typecheck, complexity, and module-size gates pass with no behavioral delta except separately fault-proven fixes. (Confirmed in this ticket's validation; no production code changed, so no behavioral delta at all.)
